chapter: Horace Henderson band and Roy Eldridge
title: Roy Eldridge leaves for Speed Webb; his brother Joe in Detroit
summary: Roy went with Speed Webb's touring band; at a battle of bands in Detroit Jones first saw Roy's brother Joe in Earl Walton's band, who scolded Roy and offered help with reading.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Where did he go on to from there?

Well, see, he went with Speed Webb in another band, a big band, that was touring. So many bands in them days was touring, you know. So he went with a big band called Speed Webb, which has Ronald Jones in it. And -- but let's see, we went to a place -- I was getting a little ahead of my story -- we went to play a battle of music while he was with the band, with Horace, in Detroit, and we was playing a battle of music with a band called Earl Walton, and they were on one stand and we were on the other, and the first time I seen Roy's brother Joe, he was playing with Earl Walton.
Yeah, playing alto, yeah. And he got after Roy and he gave him the devil, you know. I don't think
they'd seen each other for a long time, you know. So he told him that to stay around here and let me help you out with your reading, you know.

Yeah, I think he was a little older. But anyway, the -- this guy played so much with him, until some of it had to rub off, you know. He could just play anything, "Boo Hoo Jack," note for note, like Louis Armstrong, and there was a hard solo in there. I know, because I tried to play it myself and couldn't. And he could play that thing note for note and make it swing too, you know.
